facts.text: The project is an extension of the initial OpenAI gym for robotics using ROS and Gazebo.
The README marks the repository as deprecated in favour of gym-gazebo2.
GazeboCircuitTurtlebotLidar-v0 is registered with entry point gym_gazebo.envs.turtlebot:GazeboCircuitTurtlebotLidarEnv.
The documented example constructs the environment with gym.make('GazeboCircuitTurtlebotLidar-v0').
GazeboEnv derives from gym.Env and is the superclass of the environment.
GazeboEnv chooses a random ROS master port and a Gazebo master port one higher.
GazeboEnv launches the roslaunch process for the environment's launch file.
GazeboEnv writes ROS_MASTER_URI and GAZEBO_MASTER_URI into os.environ and prints both URIs.
GazeboEnv calls rospy.init_node('gym', anonymous=True) after starting roslaunch.
GazeboEnv._close counts gzclient, gzserver, roscore and rosmaster in ps -Af and runs killall -9 on each that appears.
The environment's launch file takes its world from the GYM_GAZEBO_WORLD_CIRCUIT environment variable and includes the turtlebot_gazebo base launch (kobuki unless TURTLEBOT_BASE is set).
GazeboCircuitTurtlebotLidarEnv derives from gazebo_env.GazeboEnv.
The constructor creates a rospy Publisher on /mobile_base/commands/velocity and service proxies for /gazebo/unpause_physics, /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/reset_simulation.
The action space is spaces.Discrete(3), commented #F,L,R.
discretize_observation samples every len(ranges)/new_ranges beam, maps infinity to 6, NaN to 0 and any other range to int(range), and sets done when a range is greater than 0 and below 0.2.
Action 0 commands linear.x 0.3 and angular.z 0.0, action 1 linear.x 0.05 and angular.z 0.3, and action 2 linear.x 0.05 and angular.z -0.3.
A step first calls /gazebo/unpause_physics; a rospy.ServiceException is printed and the step continues.
A step retries rospy.wait_for_message('/scan', LaserScan, timeout=5) inside a bare except until a message arrives, with no limit on the number of attempts.
A step calls the /gazebo/pause_physics service after reading the scan; a rospy.ServiceException is printed and the step continues.
step discretizes the scan into five ranges; a non-terminal step rewards 5 for action 0 and 1 otherwise, a terminal one rewards -200, and it returns (state, reward, done, {}).
reset calls the /gazebo/reset_simulation and /gazebo/unpause_physics services, waits for a scan, calls /gazebo/pause_physics, and returns the result of discretize_observation(data, 5).
setup.py declares only gym>=0.2.3 as a runtime dependency.
The installation guide requires ROS Melodic and Gazebo 9.0.0.
The README describes GazeboCircuitTurtlebotLidar-v0 as a more complex maze with high-contrast floor and walls, in which lidar is the input that trains the robot's navigation.

determinism.notes: the fake accepts and stores reset(seed=...) but its fixed start state and its deterministic per-tick range update do not use the seed, so a seed is reported without changing the trajectory; the upstream reset() takes no seed at all

gaps: the fake runs no ROS, Gazebo, physics, contact, raycast or wall-clock loop; its five sector distances are placeholders that shrink by fixed per-tick amounts, so they are not a simulated LaserScan
the upstream collision rule checks every beam before sampling five; the fake checks and samples the same five placeholder sectors
the upstream step publishes a Twist and waits for a fresh /scan while the Gazebo world advances; the fake does not model velocity, pose, collision geometry, the Twist message or ROS timing
reset(seed=...) is an extension of the fake; the upstream reset() takes no arguments and uses no seed, so seeded repeatability is not an upstream property
there is no live or sim backend: the class starts ROS through roslaunch and needs ROS Melodic, Gazebo 9 and legacy gym, which are not available to the gate and are never imported by package code

fake-only contract: live construction (never run here) would write ROS_MASTER_URI and GAZEBO_MASTER_URI into the server process's environment, print to standard output (which corrupts an MHS server that speaks over stdio), start roslaunch as a child process, call rospy.init_node in the server process and need GYM_GAZEBO_WORLD_CIRCUIT set; the legacy GazeboEnv._close runs killall -9 on every gzclient, gzserver, rosmaster and roscore of the host

the upstream step and reset wait for each Gazebo service without a timeout, retry the /scan wait without limit and only print a failed unpause or pause call, so a live step can block indefinitely or report a transition while Gazebo stayed paused or kept running; the fake models neither

the upstream reset returns the (ranges, done) pair of discretize_observation; the bridge keeps the ranges and drops done, so a reset that starts within 0.2 of a wall is not reported as terminal until the next step
rendering, the Gazebo client, the raw LaserScan array and the ROS pause/unpause/reset services are not exposed

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: after an e-stop no world step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, the fake does not advance and its last observation stays readable; the latch publishes no zero Twist on /mobile_base/commands/velocity and does not stop a kobuki, create or roomba base on that topic, and Gazebo stays paused only when each step or reset pause call succeeds, so after a failed pause or another unpause the last Twist keeps driving the base
